title: Pipeline executor architecture hardening from T4 failures
problem: T4 (overnight cron pipeline) hit four distinct structural failures during a single resume cycle on 2026-04-06: (1) the executor's lazy import of claude_subprocess loads from the checked-out pipeline branch instead of master, silently shadowing every cost-emission/timeout/harden fix that lives on master; (2) the auto_plan stage emits prose for type='test' code_spec while executor.run_test_command does subprocess.run(code_spec, shell=True), causing 'Run' to be tried as a Windows binary; (3) the planner generated a test file using pytest fixtures despite docs/standards/code-style.md mandating 'unittest stdlib only, no pytest' — the planner does not consult code-style.md or CLAUDE.md when picking tools/frameworks; (4) executor's execution_log gets clobbered on every run start, losing the prior run's per-step status (post-036790d, git log is the source of truth for committed steps, but verify/test step status is still lost). Together these mean: any change to pipeline subprocess code is silently ignored on resume runs, the new cost instrumentation we just shipped (9bbfc32) is invisible during T4/T5, and the planner is free to violate project conventions without being caught until execution time.
description: Bundle four related fixes that together restore the pipeline's ability to honor master code and project conventions during autonomous runs. (A) Eliminate lazy-import shadowing in pipeline/executor.py: either eager-import claude_subprocess and cost_emit at module load time (before any git checkout), or run the executor in a separate worktree (preferred — fully isolates the run's working tree from master). The eager-import path is smaller; the worktree path is more correct architecturally and would also fix several latent concurrency hazards. Pick one based on engineering effort. (B) Update auto_plan's prompt to specify code_spec format per action type: for action='test', code_spec must be a single shell command (no prose, no surrounding instructions). For action='verify', code_spec must be the verify prompt body. For action='create'/'modify'/'delete', code_spec is freeform pseudocode as today. Add a validate_plan check that rejects test-action steps whose code_spec contains newlines or starts with a non-command word. (C) Make the planner project-convention-aware: the auto_plan prompt must instruct the model to read CLAUDE.md and docs/standards/code-style.md before deciding on test frameworks, languages, library choices, or naming conventions. Add an explicit guardrail line like 'Never propose pytest for this codebase — use unittest. Never propose external dependencies — stdlib only.' (D) Stop clobbering the execution log on resume: read pipeline/executions/<uuid>.json if it exists, carry forward step entries with status='passed' for any step also detected by get_completed_step_numbers (git log), and merge new step results into the existing log instead of overwriting. This preserves verify/test step status across resumes (git log only sees committed steps; verify/test don't commit).
scope: (A) Lazy-import shadowing fix in pipeline/executor.py: either move 'from claude_subprocess import run_claude as _spawn' and 'from cost_emit import emit_usage_xml' to module-level imports BEFORE any git operations, OR refactor to run the executor in a temporary git worktree (e.g. .claude/worktrees/pipeline-<uuid>) with subprocess.run(cwd=worktree_path) for all stage invocations. Worktree approach also requires updating run.py to know about the worktree path so log_stage_cost / artifact paths are read from the right place. Pick worktree if effort allows; pick eager-import if not. (B) auto_plan prompt edits in pipeline/auto_plan.py: add explicit code_spec format rules per action type. Add unit test of validate_plan rejecting prose code_spec for test-action steps. (C) auto_plan prompt edits to require reading CLAUDE.md and code-style.md before making framework/library/style decisions. Add a validation hook that catches obvious violations (e.g. plan mentions 'pytest' or 'requests' or any external import) and re-prompts the planner. (D) executor.py main(): read existing log_path JSON if present, build a {step_number: previous_entry} map, and when carrying forward 'completed_step_numbers' steps, prefer the previous entry if it exists. For new step results, merge into the existing log structure rather than starting from {steps: []}. OUT OF SCOPE: actually fixing T4's existing branch (steps 5-7 still need to land somehow, but that is a content question not an architecture question), and any prompt-caching or SDK-refactor work.
context: Discovered on 2026-04-06 during the T4 resume. Four issues fired in a single 779s executor run that produced an unusable test file (pytest in a unittest codebase) and aborted at step 6 (prose-as-shell-command). T4 has burned ~1.6M raw tokens across three executor attempts with the deliverable still incomplete. T5 (portability epic) cannot safely run until at least item (A) is fixed because all of today's instrumentation work would be silently shadowed on T5's branch. Item (A) is a strict prerequisite for T5; items (B) and (C) prevent the same class of planner failure from blowing up T5; item (D) is a quality-of-life fix that lost less data than expected after 036790d landed. Related commits from this session: 036790d (executor resume skip via git log), 9bbfc32 (cost breakdown instrumentation), 24bae48 (executor retry abort + auto_plan scoping + timeout bump). T4's branch pipeline/5029f36e-35af-4923-9dd8-d9139bfde8ff has steps 1-5 committed (step 5 = the unusable test file); steps 6-7 not done; the branch is sitting clean and untouched at master HEAD time of writing this ticket.
